scenarios.topic: Ideal spanning-tree root and path reasoning
scenarios.title: Choose the intended root without cutting links
scenarios.summary: Elect the core bridge while keeping the whole redundant topology available.
scenarios.objective: Make core the root seen by both west and east. Keep every supplied bridge, port and physical link available; do not disconnect a competitor. Any valid priorities meeting those outcomes are accepted.
steps: Check current root, roles and tree path

guide.title: Understand the task
guide.why: A redundant network needs a consistent way to choose which paths to use. In this ideal calculation, bridges choose the lowest bridge identity as the root. All connected bridges agree on that root.
guide.action: Read the full assignment and inspect the current applied root, roles and physical links.

guide.title: Configure and investigate
guide.why: Bridge identity compares priority plus the common system-ID extension, then MAC address. Lower numbers win. Set bridge priorities in steps of 4096; changing a label does not change identity. An isolated bridge declaring itself root is not a successful network repair.
guide.action: Edit only the needed native fields, Apply and compare current observations with the assignment.

guide.why: Current outcomes and physical availability matter, not a previously passing check or a specific click sequence.
guide.action: Use Check work, inspect each unmet result and retry. Keep the complete graph available.

scenarios.explanation: Priority is compared before MAC. A suitable core priority wins without taking anything offline. Physical links can remain available even when some ports discard in the derived tree.

scenarios.topic: Ideal spanning-tree root and path reasoning
scenarios.title: Repair a rootward path using local costs
scenarios.summary: Diagnose a direct uplink that should yield to an indirect path.
scenarios.objective: Keep core as root. Make west use its east port as the root port, with west-to-core forwarding-tree path east-west then core-east. East must keep core as its root port and west/core must be Alternate. Keep every bridge, port and link available. Costs and priorities may vary if all these outcomes hold.
steps: Check current root, roles and tree path

guide.title: Understand the task
guide.why: After choosing the root, each nonroot bridge chooses its best rootward port. The total adds that bridge’s local receiving-port cost to the neighbour’s advertised cost. A lower total is preferred.
guide.action: Read the full assignment and inspect the current applied root, roles and physical links.

guide.title: Configure and investigate
guide.why: The cost at the other end of the same wire is a different value. Here direct west/core costs 4; via east costs west/east 4 plus east/core 4, totaling 8. To prefer the indirect path, make the direct local total less attractive. This changes the tree, not physical availability.

scenarios.explanation: An indirect path can win when its total is lower. The receiving bridge’s own cost matters; changing an unrelated sending-end cost is not the same operation. The unused direct port remains physically up and Alternate/Discarding.

scenarios.topic: Ideal spanning-tree root and path reasoning
scenarios.title: Prefer the second of two parallel uplinks
scenarios.summary: Investigate equal-cost tie-breaks and choose the requested active uplink.
scenarios.objective: Keep core as root. Make west/b the root port, west/a Alternate, and uplink-b the west-to-core forwarding-tree path. Keep both links and all bridges/ports available. You may use priorities or costs; the goal is the requested current tree, not one prescribed number.
steps: Check current root, roles and tree path

guide.title: Understand the task
guide.why: Two parallel uplinks can lead to the same root with equal cost. The next comparisons use the sending bridge identity and sending port identity. A lower port priority wins before the port number.
guide.action: Read the full assignment and inspect the current applied root, roles and physical links.

guide.title: Configure and investigate
guide.why: With the same core sender and equal costs, core/a initially advertises the lower port identity. Lowering core/b port priority can make west choose uplink-b. Lowering only west/b’s receiving port priority does not overrule the earlier sending-port comparison. A different local cost can also validly choose the requested path.
guide.action: Edit only the needed native fields, Apply and compare current observations with the assignment.

guide.title: Verify the handover
guide.why: Current outcomes and physical availability matter, not a previously passing check or a specific click sequence.
guide.action: Use Check work, inspect each unmet result and retry. Keep the complete graph available.

scenarios.explanation: Both uplinks stay available. A sending port’s priority resolves this equal-cost, same-sender case before the receiving port identity. A legitimate cost-based alternative is also accepted because the assignment asks for the resulting tree.

scenarios.topic: Ideal spanning-tree root and path reasoning
scenarios.title: Hand over a redundant four-bridge network
scenarios.summary: Combine root election, local-path diagnosis and preservation in one handover.
scenarios.objective: Make core the root throughout the connected four-bridge network. Leaf must use upper as its root port and the path upper-leaf then core-upper to core; leaf/lower must be Alternate. Lower must retain core as its root and root port. Keep every bridge, port and link available. Choose any permitted priorities/costs that meet these results.
steps: Check current root, roles and tree path

guide.title: Understand the task
guide.why: A handover can contain more than one fault. Fixing the root election alone does not guarantee that each access bridge chooses the required path. Check root identity, root-port choice and the actual forwarding-tree path separately.
guide.action: Read the full assignment and inspect the current applied root, roles and physical links.

guide.title: Configure and investigate
guide.why: The supplied leaf has a low bridge priority and a costly upper-facing port. Find the current root first, then compare leaf’s local totals through upper and lower. Do not hide a fault by disabling the lower path; the alternate physical path must remain available.
guide.action: Edit only the needed native fields, Apply and compare current observations with the assignment.

guide.title: Verify the handover
guide.why: Current outcomes and physical availability matter, not a previously passing check or a specific click sequence.
guide.action: Use Check work, inspect each unmet result and retry. Keep the complete graph available.

scenarios.explanation: A root correction and a local-cost correction solve different problems. The leaf chooses upper while its lower port discards; lower itself remains connected through core. These are stable calculated paths, not a measured failover or packet-delivery result.
